AFWD.chosen_element: definition of modular form Fourier coefficients and Hecke operators
AFWD.justification: forward morphism building the analytic machinery: `ModularForm`, `HeckeOperator`, `Newform` definitions that enable the modularity statement

AREV.chosen_element: refactoring of `EllipticCurve` API to support isogeny classes and conductor computation
AREV.justification: reverse descent: generalizing the elliptic curve structure to accommodate modularity proof requirements like `conductor`, `isogeny_class`, `minimal_model`

CLINK.chosen_element: composition of Galois representation construction with modular form attachment
CLINK.justification: sequential chaining: `GaloisRepresentation.of_elliptic_curve` composed with `ModularForm.to_galois_representation` to produce the compatible system needed for modularity

ENGAGR.chosen_element: simultaneous assumption of modularity and non-modularity for Frey curve in FLT proof sketch
ENGAGR.justification: the contradiction is held live: assuming a counterexample to Fermat yields a Frey curve that is both modular (by modularity theorem) and non-modular (by Ribet's level lowering); this B-state drives the proof by contradiction without explosion

EVALF.chosen_element: failed attempt to formalize Euler system argument for rank bound
EVALF.justification: negative arm: the Kolyvagin system machinery requires Iwasawa theory not yet in Mathlib; the proof gap is constructively identified as missing `IwasawaModule` and `EulerSystem` definitions

EVALT.chosen_element: successful formalization of weak Mordell-Weil: `E(Q)/nE(Q)` is finite
EVALT.justification: affirmative arm: the Kummer sequence and Galois cohomology bound the Selmer group, proving finite generation of the n-torsion quotient

FFUSE.chosen_element: Taylor-Wiles patching argument rejoining both tracks at the level of deformation rings
FFUSE.justification: the arms rejoin when the analytic Hecke algebra is shown isomorphic to the algebraic universal deformation ring via `R = T`; conflicting local-global compatibility conditions fuse to B (both hold)

FSPLIT.chosen_element: bifurcation into analytic track (modular forms, L-functions) and algebraic track (Galois representations, étale cohomology)
FSPLIT.justification: the modularity proof naturally splits: one arm develops analytic theory of modular forms and L-functions; the other builds p-adic Galois representations and deformation rings

IFIX.chosen_element: merged PR #12345: `EllipticCurve.modular` with all dependencies frozen in Mathlib4
IFIX.justification: permanent ROM fixation: the main theorem and its dependency closure (modular forms, Galois representations, L-functions) are appended to the library; cannot be undone without breaking downstream theorems

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: the L-function equality `L(E, s) = L(f, s)` as self-referential identity
IMSCRIB.justification: the functional equation makes the L-function recognize itself under `s ↦ 2-s`; the modularity theorem asserts the elliptic curve L-function *is* a modular form L-function — identity at the level of Dirichlet series

TANCH.chosen_element: complete modularity theorem statement with functional equation and Mordell-Weil corollary
TANCH.justification: the terminal anchor is the fully formalized theorem `EllipticCurve.modular` plus `LFunction.functional_equation` and `MordellWeil.finite_generation` all type-checked in main

VINIT.chosen_element: empty Mathlib namespace for elliptic curves over Q
VINIT.justification: no definitions of modular forms, Galois representations, or L-functions exist yet; the formalization starts from a void state

phase_2.fuse_element: Taylor-Wiles patching argument rejoining both tracks at the level of deformation rings
phase_2.fuse_result: the `R = T` isomorphism: universal deformation ring ≅ Hecke algebra, with both local-global compatibility and analytic continuation holding simultaneously (B)
phase_2.rejoin_note: the analytic arm constructs the Hecke algebra acting on modular forms; the algebraic arm constructs the universal deformation ring of the mod p Galois representation; patching identifies them — conflicting local conditions at bad primes fuse to B, not error
phase_2.split_element: bifurcation into analytic track (modular forms, L-functions) and algebraic track (Galois representations, étale cohomology)
phase_2.split_input: the modularity conjecture statement: every elliptic curve over Q corresponds to a weight-2 newform
split_outputs: analytic development of modular forms, Hecke algebras, L-functions, functional equations
algebraic development of p-adic Galois representations, deformation rings, local-global compatibility
phase_2.verdict_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.both_description: B4 B (11) — both held at once: the Frey curve in FLT proof is simultaneously modular (by theorem) and non-modular (by Ribet); the functional equation holds L(E,s) = ±L(E,2-s) with both signs possible until root number is computed
phase_3.false_description: B4 F (10) — constructively refuted: a proof attempt fails because a required lemma is missing or a definition is inadequate (e.g., Euler system formalization blocked by absent Iwasawa theory)
phase_3.true_description: B4 T (01) — constructively proven: a component theorem (e.g., weak Mordell-Weil, modularity of semistable curves) has a complete proof term
phase_3.void_description: B4 N (00) — neither: no formalization artifacts exist; the namespace is empty

define LFunction from Dirichlet series with Euler product
refactor EllipticCurve to add conductor, minimal_model, isogeny_class
generalize GaloisRepresentation to support p-adic coefficients and Hodge-Tate weights
bifurcate into analytic track (modular forms, L-functions) and algebraic track (Galois representations, deformation theory)
analytic track — formalize Atkin-Lehner theory, newform decomposition, Petersson inner product
analytic track — prove functional equation for L(f,s) via Mellin transform and modularity of f
analytic track — attempt Euler system for rank bound fails; Iwasawa theory missing
algebraic track — construct p-adic Galois representation ρ_E,p from Tate module
algebraic track — formalize universal deformation ring R for residual representation ρ̄
algebraic track — prove local-global compatibility at p ≠ ℓ via Fontaine-Laffaille
hold Frey curve contradiction — assume non-modular elliptic curve from FLT counterexample
compose GaloisRepresentation.of_elliptic_curve with ModularForm.to_galois_representation

Mordell-Weil — E(Q) finitely generated abelian group

complete modularity theorem with functional equation and Mordell-Weil corollary in main branch
